inferential-statistics.def: Statistics that use data from a sample to draw conclusions about the population it came from, with a stated chance of being wrong.

statistical-significance.def: A result is statistically significant when it would be unlikely to occur by chance alone if there were no real difference or relationship; psychologists usually require a probability (p value) below .05, written $p < .05$.

effect-size.def: A measure of how large a difference or relationship is, such as how many standard deviations apart two group means are, regardless of sample size.
